questions.text:
Consider the Boolean operator with the following properties:
[latex]x \# 0=x, x \# 1=\bar{x}[/latex], [latex]x \# x=0[/latex] and [latex]x \# \bar{x}=1[/latex]. Then [latex]x \# y[/latex] is equivalent to
questions.solution:
[latex]x\#0=x[/latex], [latex]x\#1=\bar x[/latex], [latex]x\#x=0[/latex], [latex]x\#\bar x=1[/latex]: these are exactly the properties of XOR.

[latex]x\#y=x\bar y+\bar xy[/latex]

Answer: [latex]x\bar y+\bar xy[/latex]

questions.text: The decimal number has 64 digits. The number of bits needed for its equivalent binary representation is?
questions.solution:
The largest 64-digit number is just below [latex]10^{64}[/latex].

Bits = [latex]\lceil64\log_210\rceil=\lceil64\times3.3219\rceil=\lceil212.6\rceil=213[/latex]

Answer: 213

questions.text: The boolean expression [latex]A B+A B^{\prime}+A^{\prime} C+A C[/latex] is independent of the boolean variable
questions.solution:
[latex]AB+AB'=A[/latex] and [latex]A'C+AC=C[/latex], so the expression is A + C.

B has disappeared.

Answer: B

questions.text: The number of 1's in the binary representation of [latex](3*4096 + 15*256 + 5*16 + 3)[/latex] are:
questions.solution:
The number in hex is 3F53 (3, 15, 5, 3 at powers of 16).

0011 1111 0101 0011 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 + 4 + 2 + 2 = 10 ones

Answer: 10

questions.text:
Minimum number of 2x1 multiplexers required to realize the following function, [latex]f=\bar{A} \bar{B} C+\bar{A} \bar{B} \bar{C}[/latex]
Assume that inputs are available only in true form and Boolean a constant 1 and 0 are available.
questions.solution:
[latex]f=\bar A\bar BC+\bar A\bar B\bar C=\bar A\bar B[/latex]

- Mux 1: select A, inputs I0 = 1, I1 = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] gives [latex]\bar A[/latex]
- Mux 2: select B, inputs I0 = [latex]\bar A[/latex], I1 = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] gives [latex]\bar A\bar B[/latex]

Answer: 2
